en.g: Make predictions about the future with will.
p: Form: will plus base verb for every person: It will rain. You'll love it.

en.g: Use will for quick decisions, offers and promises.
p: Instant decisions, made while speaking: The phone's ringing. I'll get it!
Offers of help: I'll carry that for you. Shall I open the window?
Promises: I'll call you later. I won't forget, I promise.
en.q: Your friend says: I'm so hungry! Offer something with I'll.
en.c: Write three offers and three promises you could make to friends or family this week.

Versprechen: I'll call you later. I won't forget, I promise.
de.q: Ein Freund sagt: I'm so hungry! Biete etwas mit I'll an.
de.c: Schreib drei Angebote und drei Versprechen, die du diese Woche Freunden oder Familie machen könntest.

vocab.ex: Someone's at the door. I'll get it!
That box looks heavy. I'll help you.
I'm busy now. I'll call you later.
I'll be on time, I promise.
Your birthday? I won't forget!
Shall I make some tea?

target.gram: Will for decisions made now (I'll take it), offers (I'll help) and promises (I won't tell anyone). Offers also: Shall I...?

en.g: Choose between going to and will when you talk about the future.
p: Going to for plans decided before: I'm going to visit Mum on Sunday.
Will for decisions made now: Oh, it's raining. I'll take an umbrella.
Evidence you can see uses going to: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain. Opinion uses will.
en.q: What are you going to do tonight? And what will you do if you have free time?
en.c: Write a short dialogue that uses going to for a plan and will for a quick decision.

de.g: Du wählst zwischen going to und will, wenn du über die Zukunft sprichst.
p: Going to für vorher beschlossene Pläne: I'm going to visit Mum on Sunday.
Will für Entscheidungen im Moment: Oh, it's raining. I'll take an umbrella.
Sichtbare Hinweise: going to: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain. Meinung: will.
de.q: Was machst du heute Abend? Und was machst du wohl, wenn du freie Zeit hast?
de.c: Schreib einen kurzen Dialog mit going to für einen Plan und will für eine spontane Entscheidung.

es.g: Elige entre going to y will al hablar del futuro.
p: Going to para planes decididos antes: I'm going to visit Mum on Sunday.
Will para decisiones del momento: Oh, it's raining. I'll take an umbrella.
Con pruebas visibles, going to: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain. Con opiniones, will.
es.q: ¿Qué vas a hacer esta noche? ¿Y qué harás si tienes tiempo libre?
es.c: Escribe un breve diálogo con going to para un plan y will para una decisión rápida.

fr.g: Choisir entre going to et will pour parler du futur.
p: Going to pour un projet décidé avant : I'm going to visit Mum on Sunday.
Will pour une décision prise sur le moment : Oh, it's raining. I'll take an umbrella.
Avec un indice visible, going to : Look at those clouds! It's going to rain. Pour un avis, will.
fr.q: Que vas-tu faire ce soir ? Et que feras-tu si tu as du temps libre ?
fr.c: Écris un court dialogue avec going to pour un projet et will pour une décision rapide.

it.g: Scegli tra going to e will quando parli del futuro.

Will per decisioni prese sul momento: Oh, it's raining. I'll take an umbrella.
Con prove visibili, going to: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain. Con opinioni, will.
it.q: Cosa farai stasera? E cosa farai se hai tempo libero?
it.c: Scrivi un breve dialogo con going to per un piano e will per una decisione rapida.

pt.g: Escolhe entre going to e will ao falar do futuro.

pt.c: Escreve um pequeno diálogo com going to para um plano e will para uma decisão rápida.

vocab.ex: I'm going to visit my mum on Sunday.

target.gram: Going to = plan made before or visible evidence. Will = decision at the moment of speaking or opinion/prediction.

en.g: Talk about fixed plans with a time and place using the present continuous.
p: Use am, is or are plus -ing for arrangements: I'm meeting Tom at eight.
There is usually a time, a place or another person: We're having lunch with Ana on Friday.
Ask about plans: What are you doing this weekend? Are you working tomorrow?
en.q: What are you doing this weekend? Tell me about one fixed arrangement.
en.c: Write your diary for next week with five arrangements in the present continuous.

de.g: Du sprichst im present continuous über feste Pläne mit Zeit und Ort.
p: Am, is oder are plus -ing für Verabredungen: I'm meeting Tom at eight.
Meist gibt es eine Zeit, einen Ort oder eine Person: We're having lunch with Ana on Friday.
Frag nach Plänen: What are you doing this weekend? Are you working tomorrow?
de.q: Was machst du dieses Wochenende? Erzähl mir von einer festen Verabredung.
de.c: Schreib deinen Kalender für nächste Woche mit fünf Terminen im present continuous.

es.g: Habla de planes fijos con hora y lugar usando el present continuous.
p: Usa am, is o are más -ing para planes cerrados: I'm meeting Tom at eight.
Suele haber hora, lugar u otra persona: We're having lunch with Ana on Friday.
Pregunta por planes: What are you doing this weekend? Are you working tomorrow?
es.q: ¿Qué haces este fin de semana? Cuéntame un plan ya cerrado.
es.c: Escribe tu agenda de la próxima semana con cinco citas en present continuous.

fr.g: Parler de projets fixés, avec heure et lieu, au present continuous.
p: Am, is ou are plus -ing pour un rendez-vous : I'm meeting Tom at eight.
Il y a souvent une heure, un lieu ou une personne : We're having lunch with Ana on Friday.
Pour demander : What are you doing this weekend? Are you working tomorrow?
fr.q: Que fais-tu ce week-end ? Parle-moi d'un rendez-vous déjà fixé.
fr.c: Écris ton agenda de la semaine prochaine avec cinq rendez-vous au present continuous.

it.g: Parli di piani fissati, con ora e luogo, usando il present continuous.

Di solito c'è un'ora, un luogo o una persona: We're having lunch with Ana on Friday.
Chiedi dei piani: What are you doing this weekend? Are you working tomorrow?
it.q: Cosa fai questo weekend? Raccontami un impegno già fissato.
it.c: Scrivi la tua agenda della prossima settimana con cinque impegni al present continuous.

pt.g: Fala de planos marcados, com hora e lugar, usando o present continuous.

en.g: Arrange a time to meet, at work or with friends.
p: Suggest a day: Are you free on Friday? How about Tuesday?
Suggest a time: How about ten o'clock? Is three o'clock OK for you?
Agree or change: That works for me. Sorry, I can't then. Can we make it later?
en.q: Let's arrange a coffee together. When are you free, and what time suits you?
en.c: Write a short chat that sets up a meeting, with one change of time before you agree.

de.g: Du vereinbarst einen Termin, bei der Arbeit oder mit Freunden.
p: Einen Tag vorschlagen: Are you free on Friday? How about Tuesday?
Eine Uhrzeit vorschlagen: How about ten o'clock? Is three o'clock OK for you?
Zusagen oder ändern: That works for me. Sorry, I can't then. Can we make it later?
de.q: Lass uns einen Kaffee ausmachen. Wann hast du Zeit und welche Uhrzeit passt dir?
de.c: Schreib einen kurzen Chat, der ein Treffen vereinbart, mit einer Zeitänderung vor der Zusage.

es.g: Queda a una hora, en el trabajo o con amigos.
p: Propón un día: Are you free on Friday? How about Tuesday?

Acepta o cambia: That works for me. Sorry, I can't then. Can we make it later?
es.q: Quedemos para un café. ¿Cuándo estás libre y qué hora te viene bien?

fr.q: Organisons un café. Quand es-tu libre et quelle heure te convient ?

Proponi un orario: How about ten o'clock? Is three o'clock OK for you?
Accetta o cambia: That works for me. Sorry, I can't then. Can we make it later?
it.q: Organizziamo un caffè. Quando sei libero e che ora ti va bene?

Sugira um horário: How about ten o'clock? Is three o'clock OK for you?

en.g: Give and ask for advice with should and shouldn't.

Shouldn't for things that are not a good idea: You shouldn't stay up so late.
Ask for advice: Should I take an umbrella? What should I do?

Shouldn't für keine gute Idee: You shouldn't stay up so late.
Um Rat fragen: Should I take an umbrella? What should I do?
de.q: Ich will schnell besser Englisch sprechen. Was sollte ich tun? Gib mir zwei Tipps.

Demander conseil : Should I take an umbrella? What should I do?
fr.q: Je veux progresser vite en anglais. Que devrais-je faire ? Donne-moi deux conseils.
fr.c: Écris trois conseils avec should et un avec shouldn't pour quelqu'un qui visite ta ville.

en.g: Talk about obligations and rules with must and have to.

For the past, use had to: I had to get up early yesterday.

Must steht oft auf Schildern und bei strengen Regeln: You must wear a helmet.
Für die Vergangenheit: had to: I had to get up early yesterday.

pt_BR.g: Fale de obrigações e regras com must e have to.
p: Have to para obrigações do dia a dia: I have to work on Saturday.

No passado usa-se had to: I had to get up early yesterday.

pt_BR.c: Escreva cinco coisas que você tem que fazer esta semana e uma regra que precisa seguir.

en.g: See the big difference between no obligation and prohibition.
p: Don't have to means it's not necessary, you can choose: You don't have to come.
Mustn't means it's not allowed: You mustn't smoke here.
Tip: don't have to is freedom; mustn't is a red light.
en.q: Tell me one thing you don't have to do at the weekend and one thing you mustn't do at work.
en.c: Write three don't have to sentences and three mustn't sentences about a place you know.

de.g: Du erkennst den großen Unterschied zwischen keiner Pflicht und einem Verbot.
p: Don't have to heißt: nicht nötig, du kannst wählen: You don't have to come.
Mustn't heißt: nicht erlaubt: You mustn't smoke here.
Achtung: Das deutsche muss nicht ist don't have to, nicht mustn't. Mustn't ist ein Verbot.
de.q: Nenn mir eine Sache, die du am Wochenende nicht tun musst, und eine, die du bei der Arbeit nicht darfst.
de.c: Schreib drei Sätze mit don't have to und drei mit mustn't über einen Ort, den du kennst.

es.g: Ve la gran diferencia entre no tener obligación y estar prohibido.
p: Don't have to significa que no hace falta, puedes elegir: You don't have to come.
Mustn't significa que no está permitido: You mustn't smoke here.
Truco: don't have to es libertad; mustn't es una luz roja.
es.q: Dime algo que no tienes que hacer el fin de semana y algo que no debes hacer en el trabajo.
es.c: Escribe tres frases con don't have to y tres con mustn't sobre un lugar que conozcas.

fr.g: Voir la grande différence entre absence d'obligation et interdiction.
p: Don't have to veut dire pas nécessaire, tu choisis : You don't have to come.
Mustn't veut dire interdit : You mustn't smoke here.
Astuce : don't have to, c'est la liberté ; mustn't, c'est un feu rouge.
fr.q: Dis-moi une chose que tu n'es pas obligé de faire le week-end et une chose interdite au travail.
fr.c: Écris trois phrases avec don't have to et trois avec mustn't sur un lieu que tu connais.

it.g: Capisci la grande differenza tra nessun obbligo e un divieto.
p: Don't have to vuol dire non serve, puoi scegliere: You don't have to come.
Mustn't vuol dire non è permesso: You mustn't smoke here.
Trucco: don't have to è libertà; mustn't è un semaforo rosso.
it.q: Dimmi una cosa che non devi per forza fare nel weekend e una che non devi fare al lavoro.
it.c: Scrivi tre frasi con don't have to e tre con mustn't su un posto che conosci.

pt.g: Vê a grande diferença entre não ser obrigatório e ser proibido.
p: Don't have to quer dizer que não é preciso, podes escolher: You don't have to come.
Mustn't quer dizer que não é permitido: You mustn't smoke here.
Dica: don't have to é liberdade; mustn't é um sinal vermelho.
pt.q: Diz-me uma coisa que não tens de fazer ao fim de semana e uma que não podes fazer no trabalho.
pt.c: Escreve três frases com don't have to e três com mustn't sobre um sítio que conheces.

pt_BR.g: Veja a grande diferença entre não ser obrigatório e ser proibido.
p: Don't have to quer dizer que não precisa, você escolhe: You don't have to come.

pt_BR.q: Me diga uma coisa que você não precisa fazer no fim de semana e uma que não pode fazer no trabalho.
pt_BR.c: Escreva três frases com don't have to e três com mustn't sobre um lugar que você conhece.

vocab.ex: You don't have to bring anything.
You mustn't park here.
You don't have to pay. It's not necessary.
You mustn't use phones here. It's not allowed.

You mustn't touch the paintings.

target.gram: Don't have to = no obligation, you can choose (You don't have to come). Mustn't = prohibition (You mustn't smoke).

en.g: Describe the rules where you study or work with must, have to, can and can't.
p: Obligations: We have to start at nine. Students must arrive on time.
Permission: We can wear jeans on Fridays. You can use the kitchen.

en.g: Talk about healthy routines and good everyday habits.
p: Common habits: exercise, sleep well, drink water, eat balanced meals, go for a walk.
Use frequency words: I usually sleep eight hours. I often go for a walk after work.
Talk about goals with going to: I'm going to drink more water. This is general information, not medical advice.
en.q: What is one healthy habit you have, and one you'd like to start?
en.c: Write a simple healthy week plan with five habits and how often you'll do each one.
